The test image shows large, bulbous, silvery-white to grayish galls on a corn ear — the kernels have been completely replaced by these swollen tumor-like structures. This is the hallmark of **Common Smut** (*Ustilago maydis*).

Key observations:
- Large galls on the ear, replacing kernels
- Galls are silvery-white to grayish, some beginning to mature
- Local infection on the ear (not systemic like Head Smut)
- Some normal kernels still visible beneath the galls

The Common Smut reference confirms the match — galls on ears with glistening silvery-white tissue. Head Smut is different: it produces black spore masses replacing entire ears and tassels systemically, with no kernel development at all.
